Before we start

Terms used in this deck

TermMeaningTermMeaning
Nodepart of the plant with one design intentDesign intentwhat the node must do, with numbers
Guide wordNO, MORE, LESS … applied to a parameterDeviationguide word × parameter, e.g. NO FLOW
Safeguardexisting alarm, trip, valve or procedureS, L, Rseverity, likelihood, $R = S\times L$
I-1, I-2SIS trips: body (feed, steam) and heaterLOPAlayer of protection analysis
IEC 61882the HAZOP standard (2016)MOCmanagement of change

Tags follow ISA letters (FSLL = flow switch low-low, AY = computed supersaturation). Rows, risks and recommendations come from the HAZOP tab, report AS-SA-HZP-001 Rev A; dynamic results are 30-min runs on copies of the model at design.

1

Part 1

How does a HAZOP team examine a design?

Part 1 · the plan

A standard, a team, a loop of questions

  1. Standard and phasesIEC 61882, four phases
  2. The examination loopnode to recommendation
  3. Team and documentswho sits at the table, what they read
  4. Guide wordseleven words, each with a row from CR-201

Step 1 · IEC 61882

Four phases, one of them the meeting

PhaseWhat happens on CR-201
DefinitionScope: saturator outlet to centrifuge inlet, the vacuum system and utilities
PreparationP&ID AS-PID-201, PFD, trip list, alarm limits; nine nodes drawn
ExaminationGuide word × parameter for each node; full recording
Documentation and follow-upWorksheets, 23 recommendations, owners, close-out

Consequences are judged with no credit for safeguards; $L$ is judged with them in place.

Step 2 · interactive · walk the loop

One question at a time, then the next guide word

The chips follow row N1.2, feed above demand: every row of the worksheet is one turn of this loop.

Step 3 · who and what

An independent leader and the right drawings

RoleBringsOTS tab used as the document
Leader, scribemethod, independence, recordHAZOP
Processintent, balances, limitsProcess, Design, PFD
Operationshow the plant is really runDCS console, Exercises
Instrument and controlloops, fail positions, tripsControl loop design, P&ID, SIS
Safety, specialistsrelief, rotating equipmentSafety layers, Relief & vent

Step 4 · interactive · pick a guide word

Eleven guide words, each with a row from CR-201

MORE and LESS give most rows; the time words are rare: record only deviations that are physically meaningful.

Part 1 · summary

What Part 1 settled

  • IEC 61882: definition, preparation, examination, follow-up.
  • The loop: intent, guide word, deviation, causes, consequences, safeguards, risk, action.
  • Consequences without safeguards; likelihood with them.
  • Eleven guide words, used only where they mean something.

The method is set. Next: the nine nodes of CR-201 and what they gave.

2

Part 2

Which nodes, deviations and risks did CR-201 give?

Part 2 · the plan

Nine nodes, sixty rows, one matrix

  1. The nodesa boundary wherever the intent changes
  2. Reading a worksheet rowcauses, consequence, safeguards, rank
  3. Coveragenode × guide word
  4. The risk profilewhere sixty rows fall

Step 1 · interactive · pick a node

Nine nodes, one design intent each

N4, the body and propeller, needs thirteen rows; N9 covers procedures: start-up and maintenance get a node of their own.

Step 2 · interactive · pick a node and a row

Reading one row of the worksheet

Safeguards are real tags and settings from the P&ID: a row names what exists, then asks whether it is enough.

Step 3 · interactive · click a cell

Node × guide word: was every pair asked?

An empty cell is a recorded decision, not a gap: the team asked and found nothing credible.

Step 4 · interactive · click a cell

Where the sixty rows fall

40 Medium, 19 Low, 1 High: the one High row is people entering CR-201 to descale, N4.12.

Part 2 · summary

What Part 2 settled

  • Nine nodes, with a boundary wherever the intent changes.
  • A row: deviation, causes, consequence, safeguards, $S$, $L$, actions.
  • The coverage table records every pair that was asked.
  • Sixty rows: mostly Medium, one High.

Judgement ranked them. Next: the simulator tests the consequences.

3

Part 3

What does the simulator add, and how are actions closed?

Part 3 · the plan

Run the deviations, then close the actions

  1. Ten deviations on the model30 min, safeguards active, no operator
  2. What the runs tell the teamalarms late, trips absent
  3. Recommendations23 actions and their owners
  4. Close-outresponse, LOPA, MOC, revalidation

Step 1 · interactive · pick a deviation and a tag

Ten deviations run on copies of the model

Dashed lines are the alarm limits: the first alarm often sits on a different tag from the one that matters.

Step 2 · interactive · pick a finding

Four lessons the worksheet alone did not show

Judgement ranks; the model times: a safeguard that acts after 20 minutes is weaker than its name.

Step 3 · interactive · pick an owner

Twenty-three recommendations, each with an owner

Instrument actions dominate: independent transmitters and missing alarms are the commonest fixes.

Step 4 · follow-up

A HAZOP ends when its actions are closed

StepOn CR-201
Owner and date per actionR01 relief device: process and mechanical
Written response, accepted by the teamClose-out sheet per action in the report PDF
LOPA for rows relying on tripsOverpressure, heater with no flow, overfill
Management of changeEvery later change to AS-PID-201
Revalidation and trainingEvery 5 years; scenarios rehearsed on the OTS

Part 3 · summary

What Part 3 settled

  • Running deviations on the model times the alarms and trips.
  • Some safeguards act late; some deviations meet no trip at all.
  • 23 recommendations, each with an owner discipline.
  • Close-out: response, LOPA, MOC, revalidation.

Rows that lean on trips go on: the Safety layers and LOPA tabs test them.

This deck

Key Takeaways

1

One node per design intent; one row per meaningful deviation.

2

Judge consequences without safeguards, likelihood with them.

3

Run the deviations on a model: timing shows weak safeguards.

4

Close every action, and send trip-reliant rows to LOPA.
